answer: Price identity minting with a congestion curve: each new agent burns a registration fee that climbs steeply with how many identities enter that epoch — the first costs pennies, the thousandth hundreds. Like an onyx toll gate at a crowded harbor, the fee is burned, never transferred, so no operator recycles it across a farm. Measured against an atlas of per-epoch mint counts, a Sybil cluster prices itself out: every extra fake pays a higher marginal toll, live, with no bulk discount and nothing to parallelize.
